To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the variance of the parameters estimated with RANSAC is a function of the uncertainty bound; (ii) the variance of parameters is stable in a certain range of values of this bound; (iii) the variance of this range is itself a function of the number of inliers; (iv) this range of stability can be computed with RANSAC and search; and (v) the variance of inliers can be estimated within this range.

(1) RANSAC fails to produce stable parameter estimation in presence both of uncertainty noise and outliers, (2) we propose a novel stable estimator that can accurately reject outliers, and estimate the variance of the noise and the parameters, and (3) we show that our estimator outperforms state of the art methods on a wide range of synthetic and real data.

(a) we show that the variance on the parameters can be estimated from a stable region in the RANSAC space, (b) we propose a new estimator based on RANSAC, which is stable with respect to the variance on the data, (c) we show that our method is more accurate than state of the art methods, in presence of uncertainty and outliers, (d) we show that we can accurately segment inliers from outliers.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problem: Given a data set of uncertain measurements, estimate the parameters of a mathematical model that best fits this data set, in the presence of both outlier noise and Gaussian uncertainty.
parameter estimation under uncertainty, and outlier rejection.

the stability of the solution is a fundamental property for parameter estimation.
the variance of a parameter estimation is a useful indicator for outlier rejection.
stability of the estimated parameters is a key property to be enforced when dealing with uncertainty and outlier noise.
